questions.q: Which of the following is not an objective of competition Act 2002?
opts: Prohibition of abuse of dominant position
questions.exp: The Competition Act, 2002 focuses on Anti-Competitive Agreements, Abuse of Dominant Position, and Regulation of Combinations. MRTP Act dealt with Restrictive Trade Practices.

questions.q: Consumers have the right: (i) to be protected against goods and services that are hazardous to life and property. (ii) to assured, wherever possible, access to a variety of goods and services at notional prices.
questions.exp: Consumers have both the right to be protected against hazardous goods (Right to Safety) and the right to access a variety of goods at competitive/notional prices (Right to Choose).

questions.q: Which of the following is not an element of the micro environment of business?
questions.exp: Trade Policy is a part of the macro environment (economic environment), whereas suppliers, competitors, and publics form the micro environment.

questions.q: Match the following legislations with the year of their enactment: (a) Industries (Development and Regulation) Act (b) FEMA (c) SEBI Act (d) MRTP Act WITH (i) 1969 (ii) 1951 (iii) 1999 (iv) 1992.
questions.exp: IDRA was enacted in 1951 (ii), FEMA in 1999 (iii), SEBI in 1992 (iv), and MRTP in 1969 (i).

questions.q: Which of the following is not a mode of foreign capital inflow to India?
questions.exp: FDI, FII, and NRI accounts are all recognized modes of foreign capital inflow to India.

questions.q: IMF has raised the quota and voting share of India which places India at the ___ place among 184 members of the organisation.
questions.exp: At the time of this specific data release, India was placed at the 13th position in the IMF quota and voting share.

questions.q: Foreign Trade Policy 2008-09 forecasts the share of India's trade in World Trade at:
questions.exp: The Foreign Trade Policy 2008-09 targeted a 1.5% share of India in global trade.

questions.q: On the basis of the size and composition of external debt, World Bank has classified India as a:
questions.exp: The World Bank has historically classified India as a less indebted country in terms of external debt sustainability.

questions.q: If the amount claimed by a consumer as compensation is Rs. 89 lacs, the case under The Consumer Protection Act shall be filed with:
questions.exp: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, disputes claiming compensation between Rs. 20 lakhs and Rs. 1 crore were filed with the State Commission.

questions.q: Which of the following does not fall within the jurisdiction of MRTP Commission?
questions.exp: Regulation of combinations falls under the jurisdiction of the Competition Commission of India (CCI) under the Competition Act, 2002, not the MRTP Commission.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a part of the economic environment of business?
questions.exp: Changes in Patent Laws are a component of the Legal/Regulatory environment, not the Economic environment.

questions.q: Laissez faire policy is adopted in:
questions.exp: Laissez-faire, meaning 'leave alone' or minimal government intervention, is a core feature of a Capitalistic economic system.

questions.q: Relaxing the restrictions and controls imposed on business and industry means:
questions.exp: Liberalisation refers to the relaxation of previous government restrictions and controls, particularly in business and industry.

questions.q: The International Monetary Fund has estimated India's contribution to World Gross Domestic Product in PPP terms for 2007:
questions.exp: In 2007, IMF estimated India's share of world GDP in Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) terms to be around 4.6%.

questions.q: The World Bank is known as:
questions.exp: The World Bank is officially known as the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD).

questions.q: "De-coupling" denotes:
opts: Indian market may be cut off from global markets so that it may not be affected by global volatility
separating the birds affected by bird-flu
questions.exp: De-coupling refers to the phenomenon where emerging markets grow independently and are less affected by economic slowdowns or volatility in advanced global markets.

questions.q: Which of the country's banking have been brought under "Sanctions by U.S.A. recently"?
questions.exp: Iran's banking sector faced severe US sanctions around that period due to its nuclear program.

questions.q: How many member countries are there in the "World Customs Organisation"?
questions.exp: The World Customs Organisation (WCO) had around 172 member countries during that timeframe.

questions.q: The concept of Small Scale Industries (SSIs) was brought to fore by the:
questions.exp: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 gave significant emphasis to the role and development of Small Scale Industries (SSIs).

questions.q: Which combination of the following factors has driven globalisation in the recent past? I. Growth of MNCs. II. Internationalisation of finance. III. Increased international trade.
questions.exp: The growth of MNCs, internationalisation of finance, and increased international trade are all primary drivers of globalisation.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Privatisation process leads to change in management with change in ownership. Reason (R): Change in management is not a necessary condition for the process of privatisation.
questions.exp: Change in ownership is a core feature of privatisation, but a complete change in management is not strictly necessary in every form (e.g., partial disinvestment).

questions.q: In which of the industrial policies were the following major changes introduced? Liberalisation of licensed capacity, Relaxation of industrial licensing, Industrialisation of backward areas.
questions.exp: The New Industrial Policy of 1991 introduced major reforms including industrial de-licensing and liberalisation of capacity.

questions.q: In balance of payment accounts, all goods exported and imported are recorded in:
questions.exp: In Balance of Payments, all exports and imports of physical goods are recorded in the Visible Account (or Trade/Merchandise Account).

questions.q: The devaluation of currency of a country is done when: (i) It has adverse balance of payments. (ii) It has favourable balance of payments.
questions.exp: Devaluation of a currency is typically undertaken by a government to correct an adverse (deficit) balance of payments by making exports cheaper and imports costlier.

questions.q: Match the following with the year of establishment: (a) WTO (b) Uruguay Round Negotiation (c) WTO Trade Policy Review Body (d) The Patents (Amendment) Act. WITH i. 1993 ii. 1995 iii. 1997 iv. 1999
questions.exp: WTO was established in 1995, Uruguay Round concluded around 1993/94, TPRB in 1997, and Patents Amendment in 1999.

questions.q: India abolished the quantitative restrictions on imports of 1429 items in 2000 and 2001 as per the commitment to which of the following?
questions.exp: India removed Quantitative Restrictions (QRs) on 1429 items to comply with its commitments to the World Trade Organization (WTO).

questions.q: Globalization is a term used to describe the process of removal of restrictions on which of the following?
questions.exp: Globalisation involves integrating the domestic economy with the global economy by removing restrictions on both foreign trade and foreign investment.

questions.q: When a company takes over another one and clearly becomes a new owner, the action is called:
questions.exp: An acquisition occurs when one company takes over another and establishes itself as the new owner.

questions.q: The MRTP Act, 1969 was abolished in:
questions.exp: The MRTP Act, 1969 was repealed and replaced by the Competition Act, 2002.

questions.q: Foreign Exchange and foreign currencies in India are governed by:
questions.exp: Foreign exchange transactions in India are governed by the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999.

questions.q: The balance of payments of a country on Current Account is equal to:
opts: Balance of trade plus short term capital flows
Balance of trade plus net invisible exports
Balance of payments minus capital flows
Balance of invisible trade plus imports
questions.exp: The Current Account balance is the sum of the balance of trade (visible) and the net invisible exports/imports (services, transfers, income).

questions.q: The following table shows cost per unit of production of two goods, wheat and cloth in two countries X and Y with no transportation cost and free trade. Which one of the following will take place?
opts: X will export wheat and import cloth
X will export cloth and import wheat
There is no enough information to comment.
questions.exp: Without the data/table on cost per unit of production, it is impossible to determine comparative advantage and the direction of trade.

questions.q: A debit balance of payments occurs due to: (i) Low imports and high exports (ii) High imports and low exports.
questions.exp: A debit balance (deficit) in balance of payments occurs when payments (imports) exceed receipts (exports).

questions.q: Match the following economic institutions with the year of their establishment: (a) World Bank (b) IFC (c) IDA (d) ADB WITH (i) 1946 (ii) 1956 (iii) 1960 (iv) 1966.
questions.exp: World Bank (IBRD) started in 1946, IFC in 1956, IDA in 1960, and ADB in 1966.

questions.q: Match the following components of Business Environment: (a) Economic (b) Social (c) Political (d) Legal WITH (i) Exim Policy (ii) Customs (iii) Social Values (iv) Business Law and Banking Act.
questions.exp: Economic relates to Exim Policy, Social to Social Values, Political to Customs/Tariffs, and Legal to Business/Banking Laws.

questions.q: Which among the following have not been opened for private sector participation?
questions.exp: Railways largely remain a public sector monopoly in India and have not been fully opened for private sector participation like telecom or power.

questions.q: VAT is imposed:
opts: On all stages from production to final sales
questions.exp: Value Added Tax (VAT) is a multi-point tax imposed on the value added at each stage from production to final sales.

questions.q: In which of the following countries the Industrial Revolution took place first?
questions.exp: The Industrial Revolution first began in Great Britain (England) in the 18th century.

questions.q: Which type of elasticity plays a crucial role in determining international trade?
questions.exp: Price elasticity of demand is crucial in international trade as it determines how export and import quantities respond to price changes (like devaluation).

questions.q: DFEC stands for:
questions.exp: DFEC stands for Duty Free Export Credit, a scheme related to export promotion.

questions.q: Suppose a Canadian firm imports bananas of 1000 and sells them for 2000. The effect on GDP would be:
questions.exp: GDP measures domestic value addition. Importing for 1000 and selling for 2000 adds 1000 to the domestic economy's GDP.

questions.q: In independent India, the first major foreign exchange crisis occurred in the year:
questions.exp: India faced a severe Balance of Payments and foreign exchange crisis in 1991, leading to major economic reforms.

questions.q: By which Act, the government checks restrictive trade practices?
questions.exp: The MRTP Act originally checked restrictive trade practices, but since it's not in the options (FEMA, CPA, Industrial Policy), None of the above is the correct answer.

questions.q: In which year the new Industrial Policy was announced?
questions.exp: The New Industrial Policy, which brought massive liberalization, was announced on July 24, 1991.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Disinvestment tends to arouse opposition from employees. Reason (R): It may increase the cost of Production.
questions.exp: Disinvestment often arouses opposition from employees due to fears of job loss (A is true). It does not inherently increase the cost of production (R is false).

questions.q: Match Books and Authors: a. India and Economic Reforms b. Development planning c. India: Economic Development d. Fiscal Policy of Underdeveloped countries WITH i. Bhagwati. J. ii. Chakravarty. S. iii. Drenz, J and Amartya Sen iv. Chelliah, R.J.
questions.exp: Bhagwati wrote on India and Economic Reforms, Chakravarty on Development Planning, Sen on Economic Development, and Chelliah on Fiscal Policy.

questions.q: Which of the following is the best example of Agreement between oligopolists?
questions.exp: OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) is a classic example of an international cartel, which is an agreement among oligopolists.

questions.q: Factor Endowment Theory of International Trade was propounded by:
questions.exp: Factor Endowment Theory (also known as the Heckscher-Ohlin theory) of international trade was propounded by Bertil Ohlin and Eli Heckscher.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The British established and developed Indian Railways. Reason (R): The British are keenly interested in India's economic development.
questions.exp: The British developed railways in India mainly to serve their own colonial and commercial interests, not primarily for India's economic development.

questions.q: Special Economic Zones (SEZ) have been created first time in the:
questions.exp: The Special Economic Zones (SEZ) policy was first introduced in the EXIM Policy of 2000 to boost exports.
